issues.legal_issue: A market-value determination based on the lower courts’ appraisal of the valuation evidence should be upheld when no breach of principle is shown and that appraisal is proper.
material_facts: The acquired parcels formed part of the same plot. The lower courts considered sale deeds and other valuation materials and fixed compensation at Rs. 80 per square yard for both parcels.
The Supreme Court found that the High Court had properly appreciated the material and that no breach of principle was involved.
issues.conclusion: The market-value determination of Rs. 80 per square yard was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The market value in these appeals depended on appreciation of the material before the lower courts; where the High Court properly assessed that material and no breach of principle was involved, the Court saw no basis to interfere.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and valuation_depends_on_evidence_appreciation and high_court_considered_valuation_material and high_court_appraisal_was_proper

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.valuation_depends_on_evidence_appreciati: The valuation dispute turns on assessment of the evidence rather than a disputed legal principle.
predicates.high_court_considered_valuation_material: The High Court considered the valuation materials placed before the lower courts.
predicates.high_court_appraisal_was_proper: The Supreme Court found that the High Court had properly assessed those materials.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition compensation appeal turns on valuation evidence that the High Court considered and properly assessed, the market-value determination is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: Where the applicable interest rate is higher than the rate awarded, interest is payable at the applicable rate on the entire compensation from possession until payment, subject to adjustment for interest already paid.
material_facts: The claimants had received no interest initially, or had received interest at 4% per annum, although they sought interest at the 6% rate prescribed under Section 23 of the Hyderabad Land Acquisition Act.
The Court directed interest at 6% on the entire compensation from the date possession was taken until payment, with adjustment for any interest already paid on compensation previously awarded.
issues.conclusion: Interest at 6% per annum was allowed on the entire compensation from possession until payment, with credit for interest already paid.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23 of the Hyderabad Land Acquisition Act prescribed interest at 6% per annum. The Court held that the claimants were entitled to that rate on the entire compensation from the date possession was taken until payment, accounting for interest already paid.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and higher_interest_rate_prescribed and lower_interest_rate_awarded and possession_taken_before_payment

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.higher_interest_rate_prescribed: The applicable law prescribes an interest rate higher than the rate awarded.
predicates.lower_interest_rate_awarded: The award grants interest at a rate lower than the applicable prescribed rate, or grants no interest.
predicates.possession_taken_before_payment: Possession of the acquired land was taken before the compensation was paid.

issues.definition: If an acquired-land compensation appeal involves a prescribed interest rate higher than the rate awarded and possession preceded payment, interest is payable on the entire compensation at the prescribed rate from possession until payment.

issues.legal_issue: A compensation award that treats its unit rate as inclusive of solatium must be adjusted when the stated calculation does not support that treatment.
material_facts: Solatium at 15% had been denied to one group of claimants because the State argued that the awarded rate of Rs. 80 per square yard included solatium.
The State suggested that the underlying rate was Rs. 70 per square yard, but conceded that on that basis the award would have been Rs. 73 per square yard rather than Rs. 70.
The Court directed additional compensation of Rs. 3 per square yard.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were awarded an additional Rs. 3 per square yard to address the solatium shortfall.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered the State’s explanation for treating the awarded rate as inclusive of solatium and found that the arithmetic did not support the amount awarded on that basis. It therefore directed an additional amount; the judgment cites no earlier cases on this point.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.solatium_claimed: The claimant sought solatium as part of the compensation.
predicates.award_treated_unit_rate_as_inclusive_of_: The compensation award was defended on the basis that its unit rate already included solatium.
predicates.stated_calculation_does_not_support_awar: The calculation offered to justify including solatium did not produce the unit rate that had been awarded.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks solatium and the calculation offered to show that the awarded unit rate includes it does not support that rate, the compensation is adjusted to account for solatium.
